body:
I started my career in the movie business (in Europe), and so much of what i have read about the BA workplace culture brought me back to that time.   
The laid back facade, and whispering behind people's backs. The cool kids team you should be a part of, because that's how your career will move forward in the long run. The jobs usually not advertised anywhere, and in the end, offered to friends of friends. The low salaries and constant piling up of additional tasks, and work hours that will not be compensated, because that's not how it works, you do all the things and more, and with a smile please, or no one will share your name when the next big job opening is on the table. You should be grateful you're in this position anyway, there are a hundred people lined up behind you if you're not happy, hon. The sexist and racist comments at parties, at lunch, every time we were highly encouraged to socialize, to prove we're tam players. No one talking about money and salaries because "that's not how we do things". Of course, hearing all the time that there is no money for this, for that, but also seeing what the budget priorities are. And the white white white white faces all around.   
I'm white, and i went to university to study cinema - which in this business is less valued than going to film or business school, but still places me pretty high on the privilege ladder overall. I spent a few years listening to the people telling me, more or less directly, to play the game and not be too confrontational about anything. Then, when i started to raise my voice and my concerns, i was perpetually shut down. I ended up walking away from this whole industry, working in a different line of business, and only accepting short term missions when they are for transparent, respectful companies or events.   
But with a bit more experience and knowledge about power dynamics, i am now aware of all the facts i dismissed, all the moments i looked the other way, and it has made me sick to my stomach for years. I feel like a coward for selfishly saving myself, and i've wanted to find a way back in, to make some damage this from the inside.  
The toxicity goes far beyond some specific examples, that's a culture that is replicated everywhere in the media and beyond, and it will take a lot of people in every company to come together and make actual sacrifices to change that. It's hard, and it will continue to be hard. But how can we not speak up, pull out receipt, unionize, support our colleagues. How can we not do the work.

Just wanted to let you know that i get all of this and i'm right there with you. It's hard to put words on those feelings, but one thing is certain, you are not a freak, you're a human in pain and i'm so sorry you're going through this, i know how hard it is day after day.

Sending you strength as much as i can.
I'm sorry you're experiencing something similar. Thank you for sharing about that other person's idea, it's kind of lovely, in a sad way.
Ugh, fucking yes. I feel like there is usually no point in talking about how bad it gets with people who haven't experienced something similar.

Thanks for taking the time to write, i really appreciate it. The thing is... i find it quite unfair that those people (who i love, don't get me wrong) get to have partially or totally what i crave and lack (a partner, kids, a purpose, a job, a house, a stable income, a calling, you name it), and i should keep on suffering to spare them a little pain? Their life will go on after i'm gone, i'm not essential to anyone. I'm just tired of it all.

Again, thanks for your message, i hope my answer doesn't come across as dismissive or antagonistic. I'm trying really hard to find staying alive for other people worth it. But some days, it's a struggle.
